source: Shared rules both engines interpret. Extend this file instead of forking engine.ts or main.c.

shops.comment: Which capture-crystal tiers each shopkeeper id sells (non-crystal items are unaffected by this list, every shop still sells the general goods). 'default' covers any shopkeeper id not listed by name, so new merchants restock the higher tiers automatically. perfectcrystal is never sold anywhere.

reputation.comment: Live range is signed. Save byte 17 stores value+100. Both engines clamp on every write. kindName is the display-name override after father revival (2.7.5); later titles (Slayer/Tamer) reuse the same hook. pricePosPct is 1% off per +rep (never free from this alone); priceNegPct is 5% up per -rep. refuseAt/freeAt are the shop extremes (2.10). heavenfallRevive (2.8) applies once, the moment beatHeavenfall first flips true (win or capture at the gauntlet grave) -- not at the original choice screen.

natures.name: Quartz
natures.theme: white, neutral: plain beasts and humans

natureTypes.note: Crystal matchups. A crystal is a property of the SPECIES, not of an individual, and several species share each crystal. The same crystal gives the species its stat bonus (always positive; a stat never goes down) and its type. Each `beats` entry means the attacker deals strongMul to the defender AND the defender deals weakMul back; every pair not listed is neutral. Quartz is deliberately in no pair (neutral to everything, both ways). Both engines interpret this; the baker emits NATURE_CHART from it.

beats.why: A lightning flash lights the dark.
Black swallows light, so the prism shows no color.

combat.note: Full rewrite of the old flat+scale damage/guard formulas. Every attack (basic, special, spell, Toxic Burst) is atkStat (str or mag, whichever the move is tagged with, raw value plus battle mods) times the move's own power rating (0.5-1.5, shown to the player x10 as 5-15). Speed is the same shape off agility: atkAgl x the move's speed rating, used only to resolve Dodge. Guard has no percentage roll any more -- Dodge is a speed contest, Block/Barrier are a flat score subtracted from the incoming hit. Both engines interpret this block; neither hardcodes these constants.

minigame.note: Special timing needle 0-100. Red=fizzle 1x, yellow=connected 1.5x, green=perfect 2x.

growth.note: Move unlocks and evolution. Basic is always known. At secondaryAt, non-shinies learn the crystal secondary (natureMoves); shinies learn shinyMove instead. At specialAt, the species special (and extra spells) unlock. Species with evolvesTo change form at evolveAt, and the evolved form also learns hypeUp then.

natureMovesNote: Leg 2.11 redesign: these no longer deal damage. 'stage' moves knock one stat (or all 3, for shinyMove below) down a statStages step on the foe each use; 'status' moves inflict one of statusEffects on the foe each use. maxPp is battle-scoped (refills every new fight, not saved) -- see statMoveCap/statusMoveCap below for the two allowed values.

statStages.note: Index = stage 0..4 (0 = no effect). Effective stat = round(base * mult[stage]); stage 4 instead sets the stat to a flat 1, ignoring mult[4]. A stage move advances the target's stage for its one stat (or, for shinyMove, all 3) by 1 per use, capped at 4 -- it never jumps straight to a higher stage.

statusEffects.note: Only one status active at a time; inflicting a new one replaces the old one. Burned/Poisoned/Confused/Paralyzed persist on the player's own CryMon until their next rest (sleepHeal); Exhausted (shinyMove only) is battle-scoped instead, like the stage moves -- see 2.11 in CURRENT_WORK.md for why.

shinyMove.note: Replaces the old universal toxicBurst. Every shiny CryMon can use this at growth.secondaryAt INSTEAD of its crystal's usual secondary move.
shinyMove.name: Overload

hypeUp.note: Learned on evolving (see 2.11): any species that is some other species' evolvesTo target knows this. Self-buff, all 3 stats, +hypePercent% of BASE (not current) each use, non-stacking (recomputed from base, not cumulative), lasts until end of battle.
hypeUp.name: Hype Up

interact.note: World interact/talk proximity is a box test, not a radius: the target's own footprint (world.json npcs[].w/h, default 48x32 human size when absent) expanded by this buffer on every side, feet-anchored the same way it's drawn (box bottom = mark.y, box top = mark.y - h). Both engines interpret this the same way; the Dreamcast port scales w/h/buffer down by its own tile size (20px vs this pack's 32px). buffer must be at least one tile (32 in this pack's coordinate space) -- at the old value of 16 (half a tile), standing one full tile directly below an NPC (the single most common way a player approaches someone: walk up, stand in front, press A) fell outside the box on the south side, even though north/west/east happened to pass because of the box's height-driven asymmetry. Bumped to 32 so every one-tile-adjacent position on all four sides, plus diagonals, is inside the box.
